title: AgentWorkflow Lakebase Architecture Specification
objective: Build a Temporal-native loan-underwriting agent where the workflow models the agentic loop and durable human-review gate while Databricks Lakebase stores operational state for UI polling, audit, notifications, and downstream Unity Catalog analytics.

selected_agent_functionality.name: Personal Loan Underwriting Agent
selected_agent_functionality.description: An agent that loads applicant credit and income signals, calculates DTI, evaluates governed policy, recommends approve, decline, or refer, and durably awaits a human review decision.
selected_agent_functionality.rationale: Fixture-backed external signals keep the focus on Temporal durable orchestration, Lakebase operational persistence, human review, and the governed Unity Catalog round trip.

scope: Temporal workflow for the agent loop.
Activities for model calls, tool execution, Lakebase reads, and Lakebase writes.
UI signaling into Temporal and UI polling from Lakebase.
Lakebase operational schema for runs, messages, tools, reviews, events, notes, and notifications.
Durable human review signaling for approve, deny, and request-more-information actions.
Unity Catalog governed policy synced into Lakebase for low-latency lookup.
Lakebase Change Data Feed from Lakebase Postgres into Unity Catalog for analytics, GDPR, RLHF, and annotation workflows.
non_goals: Production credit bureau, income-verification provider, or loan-origination integration.
Running analytical joins or aggregations inside Lakebase.

components.name: User Interface
responsibilities: Start workflows.
Send add_user_message, submit_review_decision, and request_cancel signals.
Poll Lakebase tables or the Lakebase Data API for run state.

components.name: Temporal Cloud or Dev Server
responsibilities: Persist workflow event histories.
Schedule workflow and activity tasks.
Apply retry and timeout policies.

components.name: LakebaseAgentWorkflow
responsibilities: Own deterministic agent state.
Model the agentic loop.
Buffer user signals.
Schedule model, tool, and Lakebase activities.

components.name: Model Activity
responsibilities: Call the configured model provider with client retries disabled.
Return structured ModelDecision objects.
Classify retryable and non-retryable model errors.

components.name: Tool Activity
responsibilities: Execute credit, income, DTI, policy, and note tools.
Return structured ToolResult objects.
Keep external and fallible work outside workflow code.

components.name: Lakebase Activities
responsibilities: Persist run, message, tool, review, event, notification, and note records.
Load recent context for the agent.
Use SSL and short-lived Lakebase credentials generated with off-platform Databricks OAuth service principals from the EKS runtime.

components.name: Databricks Lakebase
responsibilities: Provide serverless Postgres operational storage.
Serve low-latency UI, notification, and audit reads.
Support Data API exposure where appropriate.

components.name: Unity Catalog
responsibilities: Receive append-only operational change history through Lakebase CDF.
Support downstream GDPR, RLHF, and annotation workflows.
Own the governed underwriting policy that is synced into Lakebase for OLTP access.

execution_flow: A caller starts LakebaseAgentWorkflow with AgentRequest.
The workflow records run_started through a Lakebase activity.
The workflow loads recent user notes from Lakebase through an activity.
The workflow calls the model activity with the current messages and available tool schemas.
If the model returns tool calls, the workflow schedules tool activities.
The workflow records each assistant message, tool result, and audit event through Lakebase activities.
When the model returns a structured recommendation, the workflow records it and waits in AWAITING_REVIEW.
A submit_review_decision signal approves, denies, or requests more information and resumes the workflow.
The workflow records final state in Lakebase and returns AgentResult.
The UI, notification service, and audit view poll Lakebase tables or the Data API.
Lakebase CDF captures the Lakebase operational schema in agentworkflow_lakehouse.agent_ops as Delta lb_<table>_history event tables after it is enabled in the Lakebase UI.
A Lakebase synced table materializes agentworkflow_lakehouse.governed.underwriting_policy_limits as agent_policy.underwriting_policy_limits.
assumptions: Temporal remains the durable execution source of truth.
Lakebase is the app-facing operational projection.
Lakebase Change Data Feed is a Public Preview feature enabled manually in the Lakebase UI.
The governed policy Delta table has Change Data Feed enabled and is served from the read-only agent_policy Lakebase schema.
The default local mode uses a scripted model provider and disabled Lakebase writes for validation.
open_questions: Which identity provider and user IDs should be stored in user_id?
What peak workflow start rate and signal rate should the task queue support?
What is the maximum expected workflow duration?
What payload size limits should be enforced before data is written to Lakebase?
Should the UI poll Postgres directly, use the Lakebase Data API, or use an API service over Lakebase?
What is the workflow versioning plan once long-running executions exist?
Are Temporal Search Attributes required beyond visibility and debugging?
Should high-volume notification dispatch be a separate workflow or only a Lakebase-driven service?
Which reviewer identity and authorization claims must be retained for compliance?
What policy-change propagation SLA is required between Unity Catalog and Lakebase?
